summary: SSE connection reset with no client ack leads to misrouted fragments and incomplete conversation closure
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightAI reports repeated sessions where SSE connections experience a TCP/TLS-level reset during mid-stream. When the client attempts to resume, the server accepts the resumed handshake but several fragments (partial JSON chunks and metadata tuples) are delivered to the wrong client session. The affected conversation does not receive an explicit end/closure event and the UI shows a hung 'generating' state.

Impact: Several BrightAI users see incomplete conversations (no closing metadata) and duplicated prefix fragments appearing in unrelated sessions. This leads to user-visible truncation or noise and breaks transcript integrity. Observed in ~0.3% of long-running streams (>60s) in us-east.

Environment: Production (dedicated cluster in us-east), edge fronted by customer NGINX sidecar at VPC egress; client using browser SDK v1.4.2 with SSE fallback.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a long-running chat generation (expected duration >60s) from BrightAI private network.
2) At ~40s, force a TCP reset on the client connection (simulate NAT refresh / ephemeral proxy drop).
3) Client reestablishes SSE with resume token and sends resume request with last-event-id.
4) Server accepts resume and continues emitting fragments.

Observed behavior: On resume, some emitted fragments are delivered to other active sessions (session-id mix), and the original session does not receive the closing 'done' metadata. Some fragments are replayed as prefixes in other sessions.

Expected behavior: Resume should atomically continue the original session only, deliver missing fragments to the correct session, and emit terminal metadata event so client can mark completion.

Relevant logs / correlation IDs:
- Customer-provided trace: trace_id=trace-Bright-9f3a
- Server request IDs observed: req=ri-7c3f2, ri-7c3f3, ri-7c3f4
- Edge error sample: "HTTP/2 stream reset (0x10)" in nginx-sidecar logs at 2026-03-09T15:23:41Z
- Serving runtime log sample: "resume: accepted token token=rt-1a2b3; session_shard=5; resume_offset=2738" followed by "dispatch: session-mismatch detected for fragment seq=2740"

Attachments: HAR-style dump, minimal reproduction script provided by customer (see comments).
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate client TCP/TLS reset during streaming (e.g., NAT refresh)
Client reconnects and sends resume token/Last-Event-ID
Observe fragments delivered to other sessions and missing terminal event

2026-03-10 10:04 - Aisha Rao (Support): 'Thanks for the trace and HAR. We're escalating to SRE to check resume routing. Can you share the last-event-id printed by your client?'

2026-03-10 10:30 - Marcus Nguyen (SRE): 'Initial look: resume handler accepted token but log shows a different session_shard mapping for subsequent fragments. Suspect race during shard remapping after connection reset.'

2026-03-11 08:45 - Eng (runtime): 'Hypothesis: when a resume arrives with a recently rotated ephemeral session allocator, fragments emitted while shard remap is in flight can be enqueued to the new session routing table leading to misdelivery. Reproduction attempt succeeded in staging with enforced small remap window.'

2026-03-11 14:02 - Aisha Rao (Support): 'Shared a temporary client workaround: on resume retry wait 250-500ms before sending first resume frame to reduce remap races. Customer reports immediate reduction in misdelivery.'
investigation_notes: Timeline: Reproduced in staging by simulating connection resets with short delay between resume and server-side shard rebalancing. Key findings: (1) resume token validation and session binding occur in separate async tasks; (2) there is a narrow window where the binding is visible to the resume handshake but subsequent fragment dispatch uses the new routing table before binding is fully propagated across the shard proxy; (3) fragments have seq numbers that cross-verify to original session, but dispatch resolves to session by lookup on volatile map which may have been modified. Dashboards: streaming-dispatch-errors spike metric correlated with NAT churn events. Repro script and logs uploaded to internal gist for engineer repro.
resolution:
Workaround: Advise customers to implement a client-side 'resume backoff' (recommended 250-500ms pause after TCP/TLS handshake before resending resume frames) and upgrade SDK to 1.4.3 when released. Temporary server mitigation: enabled a short (500ms) guard window during which resume binds are held on original shard until dispatch confirms binding across proxies (rollout applied to us-east dedicated cluster 2026-03-11 22:30 UTC).

Permanent fix: Engineering to refactor resume binding to be atomic and synchronous across shard proxies; PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7821 — target for rollout 2026-03-20 with canary on 2026-03-18.

Follow-up actions: Create a dedicated e2e test for resume race (INT ticket INT-2207), update client SDKs with automatic resume backoff, add monitoring alert for resume-mismatch-rate >0.1%.

Status: Partial server mitigation deployed; customer reports immediate improvement but full fix pending.
